clue.text: Bump suppers — good exercise for the elbow?

indicators.note: to bump something is to knock it about, so the letters of the next word get jolted into a new order

explanation.surface: A bump supper gets a joking recommendation as a workout for the elbow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bump' is the anagram signal working on SUPPERS. Bending and straightening the arms in a press-up works the elbow joints, so the definition has a question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A push-up from the floor bends and straightens the arms, so the elbow joint gets plenty of work.

clue.text: Milne character shows endless delight when in a hole

indicators.note: in means the shortened delight sits inside the hole

parts.note: a pit is a hole in the ground

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: glee is delight

explanation.surface: A character from Milne shows less than total delight when stuck in a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' leaves GLE, and 'when in' sets it inside the hole; 'shows' is only a link. Milne's Hundred Acre Wood characters are the field to search.
explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne wrote the Winnie-the-Pooh stories, in which a small pink pig is Pooh's friend.

clue.text: Those who've left their chairs

parts.note: chairs are professorships, so these are professors who have retired but keep an honorary title

explanation.surface: People have got up from their seats and gone.
explanation.walkthrough: A chair is a university professorship; retired professors keep their rank as an honorary title.
explanation.definitionFit: Retired professors who keep their academic title as an honour are given this Latin plural.

clue.text: Oarsman in running to represent republic

indicators.note: running suggests movement, so the letters of the rower and the word in are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rower is in the running to represent his country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' is the anagram signal working on OARSMAN IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny state surrounded by Italy is one of the world's oldest republics.

clue.text: Intelligence source finding information in awkward cases suppressed by peer

indicators.note: being suppressed by means being held down inside the peer word

parts.note: to pry is to peer nosily

indicators.note: in means the information goes inside the rearranged cases
awkward means the letters of cases are rearranged clumsily

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An intelligence source finds information in clumsy cases kept quiet by a member of the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' gives ESSAC and 'in' wraps it round the gen; 'suppressed by' holds that inside. 'peer' looks like a lord but is the verb, to look closely.
explanation.definitionFit: A news-gathering organisation supplies reports, that is news and intelligence, to newspapers.

clue.text: Fuss about first of regular exercises, firing weapon

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the fuss surrounds what follows

parts.note: a to-do is a commotion or fuss

indicators.note: first of asks for just the opening letter of the word regular

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school exercise

explanation.surface: A row breaks out over a routine drill that involves firing a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the fuss round R, from 'first of', and the exercises; 'Fuss' is the British idiom a to-do.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled missile fired from a submarine or ship.

clue.text: Sum suitable for very young child

definitions.meaning: to add up a column of figures

explanation.surface: A sum suitable for a very young child.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means adding up, as in totting up a bill, and also a small child or toddler.

clue.text: Teacher having no time to finish bun?

indicators.note: having no means the time letter is removed from the end of the bun word

parts.note: bun is a pet name for a rabbit or bunny

explanation.surface: A teacher has no time to finish his bun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to finish' says the T removed is the final letter of RABBIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious leader is a scholar and teacher of the law.

clue.text: Building in Spain, fine one, in form of cube

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: in means the fine one goes inside the cube shapes

parts.note: dice are cubes
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fine building in Spain is shaped like a cube.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'in' puts F and I inside DICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand structure such as a large building is an imposing construction.

clue.text: Life form on Mars, one ultimately flourishing profusely

indicators.note: profusely suggests wild abundance, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the last letter of flourishing

explanation.surface: A life form on Mars is flourishing in great numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'profusely' rearranges ON MARS, I, and G (the last of 'flourishing').
explanation.definitionFit: Any individual living thing, animal, plant or microbe, is a living being.

clue.text: Fresh blow for area outside urban sprawl

parts.note: green means fresh or new, as in green wood
a belt is a hard blow or punch

explanation.surface: A fresh blow is struck for the countryside outside the spreading city.
explanation.definitionFit: Planners protect a ring of open land round a city from building, to stop it spreading.

clue.text: into ship

clue.text: Backward area home to a single moorland plant

indicators.note: Backward tells us to read the built word from right to left
being home to something means holding it inside, so the area contains the single

parts.note: an acre is a unit of area
I is the Roman numeral one, a single unit

explanation.surface: An area that backs onto a moor is home to one particular plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home to' puts I inside ACRE to make ACIRE, which 'Backward' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers, which cover moorland.

clue.text: Distrust suggestion

definitions.meaning: a feeling that someone may be guilty or untrustworthy
a faint trace or hint of something

explanation.surface: Distrust of a suggestion.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a feeling of mistrust and a slight trace or hint, as in a touch of garlic.

clue.text: They often feature in show-musical along lines of King and I?

definitions.text: They often feature in show-musical along lines of King and I?

parts.words: They often feature in show-musical along lines of King and I?
parts.note: pedigree animals at a show, and a stage musical about felines reworked in the style of a show set in Siam

explanation.surface: Songs from a famous show are reworked along the lines of The King and I.
explanation.walkthrough: Cats is the Lloyd Webber musical; The King and I is set in Siam, so a Siamese version of it names a breed seen at pet shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of pale, blue-eyed pedigree felines from Thailand often wins at pet shows.

clue.text: Ministerial appointments in linear progression?

parts.note: read as office furniture: government cabinets formed one after another in a line, a file

explanation.surface: Ministers are appointed one after another in a line.
explanation.walkthrough: A government cabinet is a body of ministers, and 'filing' can mean moving in single file, in a line; together they name office furniture for papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Office storage units with drawers are where documents are put in order, the act called filing.

clue.text: Early instances of British investment in Italy sadly testifying to incompetence

indicators.note: sadly means things go wrong, so the letters are rearranged
early instances means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Early British investment in Italy sadly showed how incompetent the investors were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early instances of' takes B and I; 'sadly' rearranges them with IN and ITALY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking the skill or means to do something is a failure of capability.

clue.text: Resisted moves to secure journalistic appointment

indicators.note: moves means the letters of resisted shift into new places

explanation.surface: Someone resisted moves to secure a job in journalism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moves' is the anagram signal working on RESISTED.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a woman in charge of a newspaper or magazine, a post in journalism.

clue.text: disapproval

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'disapproval (14)': the start of the clue is lost in OCR and no reprint or search gave it, so only part of a definition remains.

clue.text: Trudged out

definitions.meaning: dismissed in cricket when the wicketkeeper breaks the wicket with the batter out of the crease

explanation.surface: Trudged out.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means walking heavily, and in cricket a batter dismissed by the wicketkeeper breaking the wicket is out.

clue.text: Stones seen in ring, one with copper insert

indicators.note: insert means the copper is put inside the ring word

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Stones are set in a ring, one with a copper insert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insert' puts the copper symbol inside the ring, read as the verb to phone; 'seen in' and 'with' are links. The answer is a Latin plural used in medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine these are hard mineral deposits, such as kidney or gall stones, Latin plural.

clue.text: Warbler's tail visible in tree fork

indicators.note: in means the tail letter sits inside the tree

parts.note: a beech is a tree

indicators.note: tail asks for the last letter of warbler

explanation.surface: A warbler's tail is spotted in the fork of a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail' gives R, which 'in' puts inside BEECH. The definition is the fork of the body, where the legs meet.
explanation.definitionFit: The buttocks, the part of the body where the legs join the trunk, is its crotch.

clue.text: Engage in depressing activity pupils don't follow

definitions.text: Engage in depressing activity pupils don't follow

parts.words: Engage in depressing activity pupils don't follow
parts.note: the depressing is of keys on a keyboard, and the pupils are those of the eyes, which do not watch the fingers

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren are reluctant to join in a gloomy pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depressing' means pressing keys down, not saddening, and 'pupils' are the eyes' pupils, not schoolchildren: a skilled typist works the keyboard without looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Keyboard skill using all fingers by feel, without the typist looking down at the keys.

clue.text: Man mostly reluctant to become serf

parts.note: he stands for a man, a male person

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: loth is a spelling of loath, reluctant

explanation.surface: A man who is mostly reluctant becomes a serf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts LOTH to LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Sparta this was a state-owned slave, so the word means a serf.

clue.text: Relatively busy? On reflection, he isn't

definitions.text: Relatively busy? On reflection, he isn't

parts.words: Relatively busy? On reflection, he isn't
parts.note: a comparative of the opposite of busy: someone more lazy than others is not busy at all

explanation.surface: Someone thinks they are fairly busy, then on second thoughts admits they are not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' points to a comparative form, and 'On reflection' turns busy into its opposite, giving a comparative of lazy that also names a lazy person.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy person who avoids work is the comparative form of being inactive, more inactive than another.

clue.text: Put out fish, around ten pence

indicators.note: around means the fish goes round the following letters

parts.note: an eel is a fish
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Someone puts out a fish costing about ten pence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts X and P inside EEL.
explanation.definitionFit: To eject or drive someone away is to throw them out.

clue.text: Thanks to rank Emperor almost gets in

indicators.note: gets in means the shortened emperor goes inside the rank

parts.note: a grade is a rank or level

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the emperor's name is dropped

parts.note: Titus was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: An emperor of high rank nearly gets in, and offers thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' leaves TITU, and 'gets in' places it inside the rank; 'to' is only a link. Titus ruled Rome from AD 79 to 81.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling or showing thankfulness is appreciation for kindness received.

clue.text: Gilbert and Sullivan initially seen as something delightful

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Gilbert and Sullivan were at first seen as a delight.
explanation.walkthrough: A gas is British slang for something great fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, an enjoyable experience is a hoot or great fun.

clue.text: Calms daughter in chair with drug, soporific, primarily

indicators.note: in means the daughter sits inside the chair

parts.note: a chair is a seat
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: primarily asks for the first letter of soporific

explanation.surface: A daughter in a chair is calmed with a drug that makes her sleepy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D inside SEAT; E is the drug ecstasy and S starts 'soporific'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tranquillise someone with medication is to soothe and quieten them.

clue.text: Smart pen — student's given one by mum

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
L is the learner plate sign for a student driver
I is the Roman numeral one
mum, as in keep mum, means silence, which is sh

explanation.surface: A smart pen is a gift for a student from their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' here is not mother but 'keep mum', saying nothing, which is SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Being smart in appearance means being fashionable and elegant.
